findings.desc: packages/main/src/cli/command-catalog.ts:2391-2395 — HIGH: the public `lattice dispatch --help` contract still says dispatch is only for one item/finding/cluster and tells users to provide exactly one item identifier, even though the new registry deliberately supports story-only reviewer dispatches. This preserves the original C4 guidance/handler disagreement: a reviewer following help can add itemId and then be rejected by the story-only runtime contract. packages/main/src/tasks/command-catalog-smoke.ts:127-150 does not catch it because it requires the stale item/finding/cluster wording and validates each field separately instead of validating complete registry-derived example payloads/help semantics. Fix the catalog descriptions to explain conditional story-only vs exactly-one cardinality, and add a test that fails on the current help text and validates complete examples against the public command schema/runtime contract.
findings.resolvedReason: Updated dispatch help to explain registry-defined story-only versus exactly-one cardinality; command-catalog smoke validates every complete registry example against both public field schemas and the shared runtime contract.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/agent-dispatch-registry.ts:418 and packages/main/src/handlers/finding.ts:472 / :745 — HIGH: the registry exposes a denied-command matrix, but real handler enforcement is wired only into checklist_update. finding_add never calls assertRegisteredAgentMutationAllowed (it uses a lattice-review-* prefix), and finding_resolve ignores actor/LATTICE_AGENT entirely. Thus LATTICE_AGENT=test-intent can write a finding and LATTICE_AGENT=lattice-review-quality can resolve one even though both commands are denied by their registry rows. The smoke exhaustively tests the pure helper but exercises only two selected real consumers, so it cannot prove the documented claim that permittedMutations is mechanically enforced. Wire the registry authorization into every declared mutation consumer (with deliberate main/unclassified-host compatibility) and add handler-level allow/deny coverage for every command class.
findings.resolvedReason: Wired all declared mutation consumers through assertRegisteredAgentMutationAllowed while preserving unclassified main compatibility; real-handler denial tests verify no finding, pass, run, init, scope, delivery, or resolution state is written.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/cli/command-catalog.ts:2391-2395 — MEDIUM: the public dispatch help still says the command is only for one item/finding/cluster and that itemId should provide exactly one target, even though the new registry accepts story-only reviewer/delivery calls. `node packages/main/dist/cli.js dispatch --help` reproduces the contradictory contract, and command-catalog-smoke currently asserts the stale description instead of the new story-level behavior. Update description/argument guidance and make the smoke require story-only wording so the user-facing contract matches the handler and transition hints.
findings.resolvedReason: Replaced the stale item/finding/cluster-only help text and added conditional-cardinality assertions in command-catalog-smoke.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/agent-dispatch-registry.ts:418-431 and packages/main/src/handlers/checklist.ts:559-577 — HIGH: the registry mutation matrix is not wired into all declared command consumers. `assertRegisteredAgentMutationAllowed` is called only by checklist_update; review-run separately uses lane classification, while finding_add/review_pass_set/finding_resolve/init_check_set/scope_check_save/delivery_check_set do not consume the registry mutation authority (several do not even accept an actor). The exhaustive smoke at agent-dispatch-registry-smoke.ts:209-223 tests only the pure helper, so it can pass while real handlers permit registry-denied actors/commands. This contradicts CHK-002 adversarial:1 and the L4 process-fact claim that role-gated mutation consumers enforce the shared registry. Wire each gate-relevant mutation entry through a fail-closed registered actor check (preserving explicitly intended human/main paths), and add real-handler negative tests that compare story/checklist/evidence state before and after every denied class.
findings.resolvedReason: Added registry authorization at review_run_start, finding_add, review_pass_set, finding_resolve, init_check_set, scope_check_save, and delivery_check_set; exhaustive real-handler negative coverage proves denied calls are side-effect free.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/workflow-convergence-failure-remediation-execution-plan.md:269-271 versus packages/main/src/core/agent-dispatch-registry.ts:19-164 and docs/requirements/decisions/role-separation.md:14-16 — HIGH: the umbrella required design says the registry must model an item-reviewer role family, but the implemented registry has no item-reviewer entry (the valid role-class set merely permits the string), and the new canonical role-separation summary silently omits item reviewers while claiming the current contract is complete. This leaves the implemented-contract prose inconsistent with its own normative requirement and makes the exhaustive-coverage claim unable to cover that required family. Either add the intended typed item-reviewer row with phase/cardinality/prompt/evidence authority and coverage, or explicitly amend the approved requirement with rationale that item review is retired/merged into story review; keep the umbrella plan, canonical role doc, help/hints, registry, and smoke ledger aligned.
findings.resolvedReason: Amended the approved umbrella plan and canonical role document to record that legacy implementation-reviewer/item-reviewer is intentionally folded into quality/behavior and verification-intent, consistent with the accepted prompt-consolidation decision; executable smoke prevents accidental active authority.

findings.desc: concept-cleanup: typed-registry replacement is incomplete: load-bearing reviewer/evidence consumers still infer authority from the lattice-review- prefix instead of AGENT_DISPATCH_REGISTRY. packages/main/src/handlers/finding.ts:503 and :611 classify finding producers/process events with startsWith; packages/main/src/core/reviewer-read-evidence.ts:33/:194 gates read evidence with the same prefix; packages/main/src/core/flow-fact-policy.ts:108/:142 retains a prefix policy for pass-only conversion. This contradicts the approved single mechanical authority and can let registered-lane semantics diverge from evidence producers. Replace these authority predicates with the registry/review-lane resolver and add prefix-lookalike plus registered-lane regression cases.
findings.resolvedReason: Replaced all cited lattice-review-* prefix predicates in finding, reviewer-read-evidence, and flow-fact-policy with the typed registry's registered REVIEW-lane predicate; prefix-lookalike and valid-lane regressions pass.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/agent-dispatch-registry.ts:424 — HIGH: assertRegisteredAgentMutationAllowed returns null both when actor is omitted (the deliberate main-path compatibility case) and when a nonblank actor is unknown. Every real mutation consumer treats that null as permission to continue on the main path, so setting LATTICE_AGENT=lattice-review-lookalike or passing an unknown args.agent bypasses the registry deny matrix for finding_add/checklist_update/finding_resolve/init_check_set/scope_check_save/delivery_check_set. Repro: node --input-type=module -e importing the built helper and calling assertRegisteredAgentMutationAllowed("lattice-review-lookalike","finding_add") prints null. Preserve actor-omitted main compatibility, but reject any nonblank unregistered actor before handler mutation and add real-handler no-side-effect coverage.
findings.resolvedReason: Unknown nonblank actors now fail closed with agent_dispatch_actor_unknown; only omitted/blank actor preserves deliberate main-host compatibility. Real-handler lookalike calls are rejected before writes and before/after states are byte-equivalent.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/review-run.ts:36-45,97-129 still defines and enforces an independent hard-coded REVIEW_RUN_LANES list after packages/main/src/core/agent-dispatch-registry.ts declared reviewerLane/evidenceOwnership as the single mechanical authority. A future registry-valid REVIEW reviewer can pass dispatch resolution and mutation policy yet be rejected by resolveReviewRunLane unless this second list is edited in lockstep. WHY: the central concept of B-19ca is one typed authority with no distributed role inference; requiring registry AND a duplicate lane allowlist preserves the exact divergence class this story is intended to remove. Derive the review-run lane set/type/validation from registry entries (or make the registry row consume the canonical lane set, with one authoritative definition) and add a perturbation test showing a registry reviewer cannot drift from review-run acceptance. [high]

packages/main/src/core/agent-dispatch-registry.ts:424-435 + packages/main/src/handlers/finding.ts:489-493 — HIGH: unknown nonblank actor identities still bypass mutation authorization. assertRegisteredAgentMutationAllowed() returns null for every unregistered actor, so a prefix-lookalike such as lattice-review-lookalike reaches real finding_add/review_run_start/checklist/etc handlers as an unrestricted host identity instead of failing closed. Direct reproduction after build: assertRegisteredAgentMutationAllowed("lattice-review-lookalike","finding_add") prints BYPASS:null. The smoke at agent-dispatch-registry-smoke.ts:308-390 rejects lookalikes only at dispatch/read-evidence boundaries and exercises real mutation denial only for registered roles, so it misses the state-changing bypass and zero-side-effect assertion required by CHK-002 adversarial:1. Distinguish an explicit allowlist of trusted host identities (main/main-agent/human or absent actor) from any other nonblank actor, reject unknowns before reads/writes, and add lookalike cases across every real mutation handler with before/after state equality.
